To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

renal metabolism of antibody fragments is an important factor in determining the renal localization of radiolabels, and the use of radioiodinated HLM conjugated to antibody fragments constitutes an effective strategy to reduce renal localization of radiometal labels.
radiochemical design that liberates mIHP from HML-conjugate Fab fragments results in low renal radioactivity from early postinfection times.

the renal metabolism of antibody fragments can be controlled by chemical modification of the antibody fragment with radioiodinated compounds that are metabolized to radiometabolites, such as m-iodo-hippuric acid, that are excretory in nature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of radioiodinated antibody fragments for targeted radiotherapy.
the development of radioiodinated antibody fragments that would be suitable for imaging and radiotherapy.
developing a novel radioiodine reagent, 131I-labeled HML, for the radioiodination of antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the renal radioactivity levels of HML-conjuaged Fab fragments are reduced by two mechanisms: (1) liberation of m-iodo-hippuric acid from the HML-conjugate in the membrane fraction of the renal tubular cells, and (2) metabolism of the HML-conjuage in the membrane fractions.

the low renal radioactivities observed with [131I]Fab and [131I]IT-Fab were not due to the thiolation chemistry used in the preparation of these Fab fragments but were due to the liberation of m-iodo-hippuric acid from these Fab fragments.
the renal metabolism of HMI-conjugated Fab was due to the liberation of radiometabolites, such as m-iodo-hippuric acid, that are excretory in the urine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HML-conjugation strategy is effective to reduce the renal radioactivity level in mice.

the renal radioactivity levels of HML-congugated Fab fragments were significantly lower than those of [131I]Fab, which was attributed to the rapid release of m-iodo-hippuric acid from the antibody fragments.
the HML radioiodination chemistry is an effective method to reduce the renal radioactivity levels in mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radioiodination of antibodies using HML is a useful strategy to lower renal uptake and retention of radiometabolites in mice.
the renal metabolism of HMI-conjugated Fab fragment is different from that of the Fab fragment.

the renal metabolism of HPLC purified Fab fragments can be altered by chemical modification of the Fab fragments and that these alterations can be exploited to improve the renal localization of radiolabelled Fab fragments.
